item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: The fact that this has the title of the scip instead of the number in its title really bothers me.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: The solution's a fairy simple one in my eyes: Researcher R██████ and Dr. C██████. It maintains the confidentiality of the two researchers but lets the audience tell the two apart at a glance, even just seeing the names side-by-side. Any letter works, so long as the two of them are different.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Dr X and Researcher Y are not the same person. The subject expects a Dr X to exist, but does not. In contrast, Researcher Y exists but the Subject doesn't recognize them:

Subject: What have you done with Dr ███████?

Interviewer: As I keep telling you, there's no such person. You've seen the personnel manifest…do you think I'm trying to
mislead you?

Interviewer: You don't remember researcher ███████? You've worked with him a number of times before. According to him, you've developed a degree of friendship…

Subject: I don't know him. I don't know who that is.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
"Forward:"?
Don't you mean "foreword"?

Maybe abbreviating the Interviewer/Subject in place of having them fully on each lines? Kinda distracting.

I: blah blah blah
S: blah blah blah
I: blah blah blah
S: blah blah blah
etc

Also, you seem to have mixed the two a bit around.
Early on, alternatively, either ask about X and then say they don't know such person. Both the interviewer and the interviewee.
